title: Louis Armstrong's outspokenness and the alligator story
summary: Louis said whatever he wished, even in the South, such as telling Tommy Dorsey 'not too slow, not too fast, just half-ass' on TV and telling a concert audience a joke about an alligator.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But Louie would say anywhere and he'd use vile language on top of that, saying that, and down south, too. Oh, God, he used to scare us sometimes. I mean, he --
What was the reaction? Where would he say these things?

In a dance or concert, anywhere. I mean, he wouldn't -- just like he was on the show with Tommy Dorsey one time, you know, and Tommy had said -- they had a rehearsal but anyway Tommy had forgot what tempo he wanted it in, so while on stage, now, on the TV, he asked Louie, he says, "Louie, what's that tempo you want?" And Louie just blasted
out loud, he said, "Not too slow, not too fast, just half-ass."

And people broke up and in a concert, like, he'd break the spell, you know, and he says, "You know, ladies and gentlemen," he says, "I have to tell you this because I can't forget my mother." He says, "My mother sent me down to the pond to get a bucket of water and I came back without the water. She says, 'Son, where is that water?'" He says, "Mom, there's a big old rusty alligator in that pond. So she says, 'Well, don't you worry about that alligator. Don't you know that alligator is as scared of you as you is of him.'" And he says, "If he is, mom, that water ain't fit to drink." And that broke up the concert.
He always had something going, you know. And he could get away with a lot of things, you know. That was the difference.

I used to enjoy Louie a lot. And then I used to enjoy working because, just like I said before, if you wanted to play longer, you can play longer; if you didn't want to play at all, you didn't have to play at all. It was just beautiful.
